newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway C. Bank announces fixed-term deposit rate.
newsitem.headline: Norway C. Bank announces fixed-term deposit rate.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Thursday it has set an interest rate of 3.6 percent for its fixed-term deposit rate running for the period July 1 to July 14.
Norges Bank regularly announces fixed-term deposits or fixed-term loans, which usually are carried out through ordinary auction, in order to control money market liquidity.
The bank has previously announced fixed interest rates at times of instability in the money market or if the fixed term collided with a repo arrangement, Leif Eide, department head at the bank said.
Eide said the bank's announcement was an attempt to carefully bring money market rates closer to the comparable ECU rates.
In the previous auction between June 25 and July 1, the bank's average fixed-term deposit rate was 3.46 percent and the highest rate was 3.52 percent.
At 0930 GMT, Norway's three-month money market rate stood at 3.56 percent, while the comparable ECU rate was 4.14 percent.
"Following the pressure against the crown half a year ago, we reduced official interest rates almost down to German levels," Eide told Reuters.
"Now the crown is more or less normalised, but interest rates are still considerably lower than ECU interest rates."
Analysts said Norges Bank appeared to be testing the market's reaction to higher money market rates to see if it was enough to stabilise the crown.
The crown early on Thursday was above 4.21 against the mmark, but immediately recovered after the bank's announcement to stand at 4.1995 versus the mark at 0953 GMT.
